recipes.name: Lemon Cod with Rice and Asparagus
recipes.summary: Mild white fish and asparagus roasted on one pan while the rice cooks. The simplest fish plate there is.
recipes.serving_size: 1 fillet, 1 cup of rice and a quarter of the asparagus

ingredients.prep: about 6 oz each, thawed if frozen
half juiced, half cut in wedges

steps: Rinse the rice in a strainer. Bring it to a boil with the water and ¼ teaspoon of the salt, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it stand, covered, 5 minutes, then fluff it with a fork.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment or foil.
Toss the asparagus with 1 tablespoon of the oil and a pinch of salt and spread it on one side of the pan. Roast 5 minutes.

Pat the cod dry and set it on the other side of the pan. Mix the butter, the rest of the oil, the garlic and the lemon juice and spoon it over the fish. Sprinkle the fish with the rest of the salt and the pepper.
Roast 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish flakes easily with a fork and the thickest part reads 145°F on a food thermometer.
Divide the rice, cod and asparagus among 4 plates. Add a lemon wedge and parsley.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook the rice up to 3 days ahead. Batch-cook: cool the cooked food in shallow containers and refrigerate it within 2 hours. Eat it within 3 to 4 days, or freeze it. Reheat to 165°F (USDA).

freezer.text: Cooked rice and cooked cod each freeze up to 3 months; thaw in the refrigerator and reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Pack a plate for lunch: refrigerate within 2 hours, eat within 3 to 4 days, and reheat to 165°F (USDA).

recipes.kids: A kids’ plate is about half of an adult’s: half a fillet, ½ cup of rice and a few spears. Check the fish for bones and flake it; cut asparagus into short pieces for little ones.

swaps.dairy_free: Use 1 more tablespoon of olive oil instead of butter.
swaps.other_fish: Any mild white fish works: haddock, pollock, tilapia or halibut. Thin fillets cook faster.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the rice; trim the asparagus.

recipes.name: Chicken, Sweet Potato and Broccoli Sheet Pan
recipes.summary: Seasoned chicken breast, sweet potato cubes and broccoli roasted together. A classic plate for packing lunches.
recipes.serving_size: 1 piece of chicken with a quarter of the vegetables

ingredients.prep: boneless, skinless, cut into 4 pieces of even thickness
peeled or scrubbed, in ¾-inch cubes

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds.
Toss the sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon of the oil and a little of the salt on one baking sheet. Roast on the lower rack 15 minutes.
Mix the garlic powder, paprika, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Rub the chicken with 1 tablespoon of oil and the spice mix. Toss the broccoli with the last of the oil.

Stir the sweet potatoes. Put the chicken and broccoli on the second sheet on the upper rack. Roast 18 to 22 minutes, until the chicken reads 165°F in the thickest part on a food thermometer and the sweet potatoes are tender.
Wash your hands, the cutting board and the knife after handling raw chicken. Let the chicken rest 5 minutes, slice it, and divide everything among 4 plates.
recipes.make_ahead: Cube the sweet potatoes and cut the broccoli up to 2 days ahead. Batch-cook: cool the cooked food in shallow containers and refrigerate it within 2 hours. Eat it within 3 to 4 days, or freeze it. Reheat to 165°F (USDA).

freezer.text: Cooked chicken and sweet potatoes freeze up to 3 months; broccoli gets soft but is fine in a bowl.

leftovers.text: Pack a plate for lunch: refrigerate within 2 hours, eat within 3 to 4 days, and reheat to 165°F (USDA).

recipes.kids: Kids eat about half an adult plate: 2 to 3 ounces of chicken, ½ cup of sweet potato and a few florets. Cut chicken into small pieces for young children.

swaps.thighs: Use boneless chicken thighs; they also need 165°F and stay juicy.
swaps.potato: Use white potatoes instead of sweet potatoes.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the vegetables and season the chicken.

recipes.name: Sirloin Steak, Baked Potato and Green Beans
recipes.summary: A steakhouse plate at home: seared top sirloin, a fluffy baked potato and buttery green beans.
recipes.serving_size: about 5 oz of steak, 1 potato and a quarter of the beans
equipment: saucepan with a steamer basket or lid
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Prick each potato a few times with a fork and set them on a baking sheet. Bake 50 to 60 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
About 20 minutes before the potatoes are done, pat the steak dry and season it with ¾ teaspoon of the salt and the pepper. Let it sit while the skillet heats.

Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the steak 4 to 5 minutes per side, until it reads at least 145°F in the center on a food thermometer. Move it to a board and let it rest 3 minutes (USDA).
Meanwhile, steam the green beans over simmering water 5 to 7 minutes, until bright green and tender. Toss them with the butter, garlic and the rest of the salt.
Slice the steak across the grain. Split the potatoes and top with sour cream and green onions if you like. Divide everything among 4 plates.
recipes.make_ahead: Bake the potatoes up to 3 days ahead and reheat them. Batch-cook: cool the cooked food in shallow containers and refrigerate it within 2 hours. Eat it within 3 to 4 days, or freeze it. Reheat to 165°F (USDA).

freezer.text: Steak is best fresh; sliced leftover steak freezes up to 3 months for stir-fries or tacos.

leftovers.text: Slice cold steak for a salad or a wrap; refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA).

recipes.kids: A kids’ plate: 2 to 3 ounces of thinly sliced steak, cut small, half a potato and a few beans. Kids can scrub potatoes and snap the ends off the beans.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil on the beans and skip the sour cream.
swaps.spinach: Serve a spinach salad instead of green beans.

prep_day.ahead: Bake the potatoes; trim the beans.

recipes.name: Eggs, Oatmeal and Berries
recipes.summary: A warm breakfast plate: creamy oatmeal with berries and two eggs on the side. Ready in under 20 minutes.
recipes.serving_size: 2 eggs, 1 cup of oatmeal and ½ cup of berries

ingredients.prep: or sliced strawberries, fresh or frozen

steps: Bring the milk, water and salt just to a simmer in the saucepan. Stir in the oats and cinnamon and cook over medium-low heat 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and creamy.

While the oats cook, melt the butter in the skillet over medium heat. Crack in the eggs and cook them the way your family likes (fried, scrambled or over easy) until the whites and yolks are firm. Scrambled eggs and egg dishes are done at 160°F (USDA).
Spoon the oatmeal into bowls, top with the berries and a drizzle of honey if you like, and serve the eggs alongside with a little pepper.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook a big pot of oatmeal and keep it in the refrigerator up to 4 days; reheat with a splash of milk. Hard-cook eggs ahead: they keep a week in the refrigerator (USDA).

freezer.text: Cooked oatmeal freezes in portions up to 3 months. Don’t freeze eggs in the shell.

recipes.kids: Kids eat about half: 1 egg, ½ cup of oatmeal and a handful of berries. For children under 4, cut blueberries into smaller pieces. Skip honey for babies under 1 year.

swaps.dairy_free: Make the oatmeal with water or soy milk and cook the eggs in oil.

prep_day.ahead: Cook a pot of oatmeal; hard-cook eggs.

recipes.name: Ground Beef, Rice and Pepper Plates
recipes.summary: Lean ground beef browned with sweet peppers and onion, mildly spiced, over white rice. Freezes well in single plates.
recipes.serving_size: about 1½ cups of beef and peppers with 1 cup of rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a strainer. Bring it to a boil with the water and ¼ teaspoon of the salt, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it stand, covered, 5 minutes, then fluff it with a fork.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the peppers and onion 5 to 6 minutes, until they soften and brown at the edges. Move them to a plate.
Add the beef to the skillet and break it up. Cook 6 to 8 minutes, until no pink remains and it reads 160°F on a food thermometer. Spoon off extra fat.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika, the rest of the salt and the pepper and cook 1 minute. Return the peppers and onion and toss to heat through.
Serve over the rice.
recipes.make_ahead: Batch-cook: cool the cooked food in shallow containers and refrigerate it within 2 hours. Eat it within 3 to 4 days, or freeze it. Reheat to 165°F (USDA).

freezer.text: Freeze single plates of beef and rice up to 3 months. Thaw in the refrigerator and reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Pack a plate for lunch: refrigerate within 2 hours, eat within 3 to 4 days, and reheat to 165°F (USDA).

recipes.kids: Kids eat about half: ½ cup of the beef and peppers and ½ cup of rice. Cut pepper strips small for little ones, or keep a few raw strips for dipping.

swaps.turkey: Use ground turkey; cook it to 165°F.
swaps.brown_rice: Use brown rice; simmer it about 40 minutes with a little more water.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the rice and slice the vegetables.

recipes.name: Salmon, Quinoa and Garlic Spinach
recipes.summary: Baked salmon with fluffy quinoa and spinach wilted with garlic and lemon. Rich in protein and good fats.
recipes.serving_size: 1 fillet, ¾ cup of quinoa and a quarter of the spinach
steps: Rinse the quinoa well in a fine strainer. Bring it to a boil with the water, cover, and simmer on low 15 minutes. Let it stand, covered, 5 minutes, then fluff it.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Set the salmon skin side down on a lined baking sheet, brush with 1 tablespoon of oil and season with the salt and pepper.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the thickest part reads 145°F on a food thermometer and flakes easily. Squeeze the lemon juice over it.

Meanwhile, warm the remaining oil and the garlic in the skillet over medium heat until the garlic sizzles, about 1 minute. Add the spinach a handful at a time and toss until just wilted, 2 to 3 minutes. Season with the salt.
Divide the quinoa, salmon and spinach among 4 plates with lemon wedges.
recipes.make_ahead: Cook the quinoa up to 4 days ahead. Batch-cook: cool the cooked food in shallow containers and refrigerate it within 2 hours. Eat it within 3 to 4 days, or freeze it. Reheat to 165°F (USDA).

freezer.text: Cooked quinoa freezes up to 3 months. Cooked salmon freezes up to 3 months but is best fresh.

leftovers.text: Flake cold salmon over the quinoa for lunch; refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA).

recipes.kids: Kids eat about half a fillet and ½ cup of quinoa. Run a finger along the salmon to find pin bones and pull them out. Some kids prefer spinach raw, in a few leaves.

swaps.rice: Use rice or couscous instead of quinoa.
swaps.greens: Use kale or chard; cook them a few minutes longer.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the quinoa; wash the spinach.

recipes.name: Garlic Chicken, Rice and Broccoli
recipes.summary: Pan-seared chicken with a little garlic, white rice and steamed broccoli. The plate meal-preppers make by the dozen.
recipes.serving_size: a quarter of the chicken, 1 cup of rice and 1 cup of broccoli
equipment: steamer basket or a pot with a lid
steps: Rinse the rice in a strainer. Bring it to a boil with the water and ¼ teaspoon of the salt, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it stand, covered, 5 minutes, then fluff it with a fork.
Season the chicken with the garlic powder, oregano, salt and pepper. Wash your hands and the cutting board after handling raw chicken.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the cutlets 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and 165°F in the thickest part on a food thermometer. Let them rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Steam the broccoli over simmering water 4 to 5 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Toss with the soy sauce or lemon.
Divide the rice, chicken and broccoli among 4 plates or containers.
recipes.make_ahead: Batch-cook: cool the cooked food in shallow containers and refrigerate it within 2 hours. Eat it within 3 to 4 days, or freeze it. Reheat to 165°F (USDA).

freezer.text: Freeze plates of chicken and rice up to 3 months; steam the broccoli fresh if you can.

leftovers.text: Pack a plate for lunch: refrigerate within 2 hours, eat within 3 to 4 days, and reheat to 165°F (USDA).

recipes.kids: Kids eat about half: 2 to 3 ounces of chicken cut small, ½ cup of rice and a few florets. Kids can tear broccoli into florets.

swaps.gluten_free: Use lemon instead of soy sauce, or a gluten-free tamari.
swaps.veg: Use green beans or asparagus instead of broccoli.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the rice; cut the chicken and broccoli.

recipes.name: Egg and Veggie Scramble with Toast
recipes.summary: Whole eggs and egg whites scrambled with onion, peppers and mushrooms, with whole-wheat toast. Quick, filling and cheap.
recipes.serving_size: about 1 cup of scramble and 1 slice of toast
steps: Whisk the eggs, egg whites, ¼ teaspoon of the salt and the pepper in a bowl.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion, pepper and mushrooms with the rest of the salt 6 to 7 minutes, until soft and the mushroom liquid cooks off.
Pour in the eggs. Stir slowly with a spatula until they are set with no liquid egg left, 2 to 3 minutes; egg dishes are done at 160°F (USDA). Sprinkle on cheese if you like.
Serve with the toast.
recipes.make_ahead: Chop the vegetables up to 3 days ahead and keep them in the refrigerator. Cooked scramble keeps 3 to 4 days; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Cooked scramble freezes up to 2 months for breakfast burritos; thaw in the refrigerator.

leftovers.text: Roll leftover scramble in a tortilla for lunch; refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA).

recipes.kids: Kids eat about half: ½ cup of scramble and half a slice of toast. Kids can crack eggs into a bowl and whisk (wash hands after).

swaps.whole_eggs: Use 9 whole eggs instead of eggs plus whites.
